hypothesis: B2 maker-positive rows whose hedge coherence depends on one-token low-Jaccard semantic links are more likely to be structurally spurious than rows supported by same-event or multi-token semantic relations.
interpretation: The highest quoted maker edge in the current B2 snapshot fails the bounded strong-relation ablation because three of six hedge links rely on only one shared token with Jaccard scores between 0.0833 and 0.1111.

The remaining relation-strong maker-positive row has only about 4.8 bps quoted maker edge and a scenario break-even full-bundle completion hurdle of about 84.84% if incomplete execution falls back to the quoted taker economics.
Static maker positivity is not promotion evidence; direct B2 event-time fill, forced-completion, latency and markout evidence remains required.

required_chronological_ablation.challenger: same-event hard plus semantic score >=0.20 and >=2 shared content tokens; category cannot independently authorize a hedge
metrics: completed bundle rate and one-sided fill loss
required_chronological_ablation.promotion_rule: positive incremental realized net paper PnL versus incumbent on common chronological windows at all three cost levels, with existing OOS/risk gates unchanged
